transcript: Transcript: Good afternoon, families. This is a reminder from the front office about Thursday's early dismissal. Because of parent-teacher conferences, all students will be dismissed at twelve fifteen instead of three. Lunch will still be served, starting at eleven, so students will eat before they leave. Bus riders will be picked up at twelve fifteen on the regular routes, about two hours and forty-five minutes earlier than usual; please make sure someone is at the stop, because drivers will bring younger children back to the school if no one is there to meet them. The after-school program will open at twelve fifteen rather than three and will run until its normal closing time of six, but only for students who are already enrolled; we cannot accept drop-ins on Thursday. Car-line pickup also begins at twelve fifteen; please do not arrive before noon, as the lot will be in use for the lunch period. Conferences run from one to seven, and families who have not yet signed up can still do so on the school website until Wednesday evening. Thank you.

options.A: They should plan to collect their child early instead

options.D: They will be assigned a slot somewhere between one and seven

transcript: Transcript: Attention library patrons. Beginning Monday the fourteenth, the main library will move to extended hours for the exam period, staying open until two a.m. on weeknights instead of the usual midnight. Weekend hours do not change. Please note that after ten p.m., entry is through the north doors only, and you will need to show a current student or staff card; visitor passes are not valid after ten. The third-floor group study rooms can still be reserved online, but reservations made for the extended-hours window are limited to two hours instead of the usual four, so that more groups get a turn. The café on the ground floor will close at nine as usual, though the vending machines near the north entrance will be restocked every night. Extended hours end on Friday the twenty-fifth, the last day of exams. If you leave a bag unattended after ten, security will move it to the front desk, so please keep your belongings with you. Thank you, and good luck with your exams.

transcript: Transcript: Good morning, everyone. A quick notice from facilities about the parking garage. Levels two and three will be resurfaced over the next two weekends, beginning this Friday evening at six. During that time those levels will be closed, and the roughly one hundred vehicles normally assigned there will need to park elsewhere. Staff with a level-two or level-three permit may use the overflow lot on Carter Street at no charge; just show your permit to the attendant. Level one and the surface lot remain open, but they are reserved for visitors and for staff with accessibility permits, as usual, so please do not park there even if you see a space. Any vehicle left on levels two or three after six on Friday will be towed at the owner's expense. Motorcycles and bicycles are not affected; the bike cage on level one stays open. Work should finish by Sunday night each weekend, and the levels will reopen on Monday morning. If rain delays the work, we will send an email on Sunday afternoon. Thanks for your patience.

options.B: It will be left there until the levels reopen on Monday

options.D: It will be towed, and the owner will pay the cost

transcript: Transcript: Hello, this is a message for patients of the Westbrook family practice. Flu vaccinations are now available. Patients over sixty-five and anyone with a chronic condition on file can walk in on any weekday between nine and eleven in the morning without an appointment; just check in at the front desk. All other patients need to book a slot, either online through the patient portal or by calling the office, and appointments are available on weekday afternoons and on Saturday mornings. Please bring your insurance card; most plans cover the vaccine fully, and for those that do not, the cost is twenty-five dollars, payable by card only. If you have had a fever in the past forty-eight hours, please wait until you have been well for two full days before coming in. Children under nine who are getting the vaccine for the first time will need a second dose four weeks later, and we will schedule that before you leave. Our supply is limited this month, so we ask that you keep your appointment or cancel at least a day ahead.
question: Who can get the vaccine without booking an appointment?

options.A: Children under nine who are receiving their first dose
options.B: Patients over sixty-five and those with a chronic condition on file
options.C: Anyone who checks in at the front desk before eleven
options.D: Patients whose insurance plan covers the vaccine fully

transcript: Transcript: Good evening, residents. This is a notice from building management about a scheduled water shutoff. On Wednesday the plumbing contractor will replace the main shutoff valve, and water to the entire building will be off from nine in the morning until approximately three in the afternoon. Water in the laundry room and the fitness center will also be off during that time. Please fill any containers you will need beforehand, and avoid running dishwashers or washing machines that morning; if a cycle is interrupted, the machine can be damaged when pressure returns. When the water comes back on, run your cold tap for two or three minutes to clear any discoloration before drinking. Residents on floors ten and above may notice lower pressure for the rest of the day; that is normal and should resolve by evening. If it has not by Thursday morning, please submit a maintenance request through the resident portal rather than calling the office, so that we can track it. Contractors will not need to enter any units. The garage and elevators are not affected. We apologize for the inconvenience.
question: How long is the water expected to be off on Wednesday?

options.A: From nine in the morning until sometime in the evening
options.B: From Wednesday morning until Thursday morning at the latest
options.C: For two or three minutes after the valve is replaced
options.D: From nine in the morning until about three in the afternoon

transcript: Transcript: Welcome to the museum. A few notes for today's visitors. The special exhibition on the second floor uses timed entry. Your general admission ticket does not include it; you will need a separate timed ticket, which is free for members and eight dollars for everyone else. Timed tickets can be picked up at the information desk, and the last entry to the exhibition is at four thirty, one hour before the museum closes. Groups of ten or more must book their entry time in advance through the group sales office and cannot be accommodated at the desk. Photography without flash is allowed in the permanent galleries but not inside the special exhibition, where all cameras and phones must be put away. Large bags, umbrellas, and backpacks must be checked in the coat room on the lower level before you enter the special exhibition; they are allowed in the rest of the building. The café is open until four, and the museum shop stays open until closing. Children under twelve must be accompanied by an adult on the second floor. Enjoy your visit.
question: What does a museum member need in order to see the special exhibition?

options.A: A free timed ticket from the information desk
options.B: A ticket bought for eight dollars at the desk
options.C: Nothing beyond a general admission ticket
options.D: A booking made through the group sales office

transcript: Transcript: This is a notice from the city permits office. Starting on the first of next month, all applications for residential building permits must be submitted online through the city's permit portal; paper applications will no longer be accepted at the counter. Applications already submitted on paper before that date will continue to be processed as usual and do not need to be resubmitted. Commercial permits and sign permits are not part of this change yet and will still be accepted at the counter until further notice. To use the portal you will need to create an account with a valid email address, and you will then be able to track your application's status and upload revised drawings without coming in. Payment can be made online by card, or, if you prefer to pay by check, you can still bring the check to the counter and reference your application number. Staff will be available at the counter on Tuesday and Thursday mornings to help first-time users set up an account and upload documents. Review times are expected to shorten by about a week once the change takes effect.

options.A: They will be reviewed faster than paper ones were
options.B: They will be handled after the paper backlog is cleared
options.C: They cannot be changed once they have been submitted
options.D: They can only be paid for by card, not by check

transcript: Transcript: This is a service notice for riders of the number twelve and number forty bus routes. Starting this Saturday, and continuing for about six weeks, Harbor Street will be closed between Fifth and Ninth Avenues for water main replacement. During the closure, the number twelve will detour along Mill Road and will not serve the stops at Sixth and Eighth. Riders for those stops should use the temporary stop on Mill Road at Seventh, which is about a five-minute walk away. The number forty is affected only on weekdays; on weekends it keeps its regular route, because the contractor is not working then and one lane is reopened. Both routes are expected to run about ten minutes behind schedule during peak hours, so please allow extra time. Fares and transfers are unchanged, and the detour will be shown on the real-time map in the transit app. If the work finishes early, regular service will resume without further notice. We apologize for the inconvenience.
question: Which stops will the number twelve bus not serve during the closure?

options.A: The stops at Sixth and Eighth on Harbor Street
options.B: The stops it normally shares with the number forty
options.C: All of the stops between Fifth and Ninth Avenues
options.D: The temporary stop on Mill Road at Seventh

transcript: Transcript: Good evening, residents. This is a notice from building management about a scheduled water shutoff. On Wednesday the plumbing contractor will replace the main shutoff valve, and water to the entire building will be off from nine in the morning until approximately three in the afternoon. Water in the laundry room and the fitness center will also be off during that time. Please fill any containers you will need beforehand, and avoid running dishwashers or washing machines that morning; if a cycle is interrupted, the machine can be damaged when pressure returns. When the water comes back on, run your cold tap for two or three minutes to clear any discoloration before drinking. Residents on floors ten and above may notice lower pressure for the rest of the day; that is normal and should resolve by evening. If it has not by Thursday morning, please submit a maintenance request through the resident portal rather than calling the office, so that we can track it. Contractors will not need to enter any units. The garage and elevators are not affected. We apologize for the inconvenience.
question: What should a resident on the twelfth floor do if the pressure is still low on Thursday?

options.A: Run the cold tap for two or three minutes
options.B: Call the management office as soon as possible
options.C: Submit a request through the resident portal
options.D: Wait until evening for it to resolve on its own

transcript: Transcript: Hello, this is a message for patients of the Westbrook family practice. Flu vaccinations are now available. Patients over sixty-five and anyone with a chronic condition on file can walk in on any weekday between nine and eleven in the morning without an appointment; just check in at the front desk. All other patients need to book a slot, either online through the patient portal or by calling the office, and appointments are available on weekday afternoons and on Saturday mornings. Please bring your insurance card; most plans cover the vaccine fully, and for those that do not, the cost is twenty-five dollars, payable by card only. If you have had a fever in the past forty-eight hours, please wait until you have been well for two full days before coming in. Children under nine who are getting the vaccine for the first time will need a second dose four weeks later, and we will schedule that before you leave. Our supply is limited this month, so we ask that you keep your appointment or cancel at least a day ahead.
question: When can a patient who must book an appointment come in?

options.A: On weekday mornings between nine and eleven
options.B: On Saturday mornings only, through the portal
options.C: On weekday afternoons and Saturday mornings
options.D: On any weekday, by calling the office first

transcript: Transcript: Good morning, everyone. A quick notice from facilities about the parking garage. Levels two and three will be resurfaced over the next two weekends, beginning this Friday evening at six. During that time those levels will be closed, and the roughly one hundred vehicles normally assigned there will need to park elsewhere. Staff with a level-two or level-three permit may use the overflow lot on Carter Street at no charge; just show your permit to the attendant. Level one and the surface lot remain open, but they are reserved for visitors and for staff with accessibility permits, as usual, so please do not park there even if you see a space. Any vehicle left on levels two or three after six on Friday will be towed at the owner's expense. Motorcycles and bicycles are not affected; the bike cage on level one stays open. Work should finish by Sunday night each weekend, and the levels will reopen on Monday morning. If rain delays the work, we will send an email on Sunday afternoon. Thanks for your patience.
question: Where should an employee with a level-three permit park while the work is going on?

options.A: On level two, once it has been resurfaced
options.B: On level one, next to the bike cage
options.C: In the surface lot beside the garage
options.D: In the overflow lot on Carter Street

transcript: Transcript: Attention library patrons. Beginning Monday the fourteenth, the main library will move to extended hours for the exam period, staying open until two a.m. on weeknights instead of the usual midnight. Weekend hours do not change. Please note that after ten p.m., entry is through the north doors only, and you will need to show a current student or staff card; visitor passes are not valid after ten. The third-floor group study rooms can still be reserved online, but reservations made for the extended-hours window are limited to two hours instead of the usual four, so that more groups get a turn. The café on the ground floor will close at nine as usual, though the vending machines near the north entrance will be restocked every night. Extended hours end on Friday the twenty-fifth, the last day of exams. If you leave a bag unattended after ten, security will move it to the front desk, so please keep your belongings with you. Thank you, and good luck with your exams.
question: How long can a group study room be reserved during the extended-hours window?

options.A: For up to four hours at a time
options.B: Until the café closes at nine p.m.
options.C: Until the building closes at two a.m.
options.D: For up to two hours at a time
